specs.approach: Fully additive and low-risk. (1) New sibling key 'leavedesk_caps_v1' via loadCaps/saveCaps built to the exact loadWeekOff/saveWeekOff template — leavedesk_v3 record shape is untouched, so no drop-on-normalize trap (coerceShape @883 stays as-is). (2) Store resolution is authoritative from the CENTRAL master (getCentralEmployees @2014 already exists) using the proven grooming resolver logic (helios→HEMW, titan→WLMHW, else ''), NOT lv.employees[].store — because the bridge only back-fills store on NEW seeds and existing lv.employees rows have none. A per-render name→code map (lvStoreMap) avoids re-parsing the master per record. (3) The view counts isActiveLeave records (pending+approved, matching getCapacity's dayUsed=leaves.length head-count semantics; rejected excluded) per store and compares to the store cap. (4) It is ADVISORY/display-only: it does NOT alter getCapacity/canAddLeave (@1240/1257), so the global MAX_DAY=3 add-gate is unchanged and adding leave is never newly blocked. (5) Reusable helpers (loadCaps, lvStoreCode/lvStoreMap, storeLeaveTallyForDay) are the base P1-30 builds on — spec them with an optional pre-built-map param so P1-30 can loop a month cheaply.
specs.ui: PRIMARY surface = DAY MODAL. A new 'Per-Store Leave Load' section is inserted directly under the existing 'Leave Capacity (per shift)' grid (they are DIFFERENT axes — shift AM/PM vs store — so a distinct heading avoids confusion). It renders one reused .capacity-slot per store: 'Titan World  2 / 3' with a fill bar; when used>cap the count/fill go red ('full' class) with a '⚠ Over capacity' note, otherwise 'N slot(s) free'. Any staff whose store can't be resolved appear in a separate neutral 'Unassigned' slot ('2 staff — store not set; open Staff Master') that is never flagged over/under. CONFIG surface = Staff Master overlay (#empOverlay): a new panel matching the existing Weekly-Off panel, with two number inputs (Titan World / WLMHW and Helios / HEMW), a 'Save Store Caps' button, and a hint that it is advisory-only and store comes from the central Employee Master. Recommend NOT adding a stats-strip tile in P1-28 (leave the month-level surface to P1-30 to avoid a shared-DOM collision).
edgeCases: Name mismatch between a leave record's name and the master name: resolver trims+lowercases both sides; no match => '' (Unassigned), shown in the neutral slot, not counted against either store.
Central master absent/empty: getCentralEmployees() returns [] => every head lands in Unassigned; per-store slots show 0/ cap; nothing is falsely flagged over.

Same person split across half_day_am + half_day_pm on one day = 2 records => counts as 2 heads for that store, exactly mirroring getCapacity dayUsed=leaves.length. Note this in copy is optional; keep semantics consistent with the existing per-shift grid.
Rejected leaves excluded (isActiveLeave); pending INCLUDED (they occupy capacity) — consistent with getCapacity.
cap = 0 is a valid config (means 'nobody should be off'): any head => immediately over; do not treat 0 as 'unset'.
Negative / NaN / decimal cap input: saveCaps clamps via Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number(x)||0)).
Partial/hand-edited leavedesk_caps_v1 (missing one store, wrong type): loadCaps defaults each field independently, never returns NaN.
Past-date (read-only) view: the day-modal store section is display-only (fine); saveStoreCapsFromUI is guardReadOnly()-gated like saveWeekOffFromUI.
Store master row exists but e.store is blank / an unrecognized string: st.indexOf checks fail => '' (Unassigned) — matches grmStoreCode.

Person on leave whose master row is active:false: getCentralEmployees is read as-is (fillEmpIdSelect filters active elsewhere, but the resolver should map by name regardless of active so a currently-inactive-but-on-record staff still resolves to their store).

specs.item: P1-30 — "Next 7 days" staffing strip in the LEAVE module
specs.summary: Add a compact, read-only horizontal strip of the next 7 calendar days (anchored on the shell as-of/today date via getAsOf(), NOT calendar month navigation), each cell showing heads-on-leave vs available headcount/capacity, with visual marks for understaffed days, non-trading weekly-off days, and (feature-detected) blackout days. Purely additive and low-risk: ONE new HTML container, ONE new CSS block, ONE new render function renderStaffStrip(), and ONE call appended to renderCalendar()'s tail so it stays in sync with every mutation/nav/st-date path. NO new localStorage key and NO record-shape change — it CONSUMES P1-28's per-store store resolver + caps, and degrades gracefully (store-agnostic day view, no false "understaffed" reds) when those helpers or the caps key are absent. All claims grounded in _extracted_modules/leave.html as read.

functionsToTouch.line: add a new function near renderStats (@1523); it is a function declaration so hoisting makes call-before-definition safe
functionsToTouch.change: New read-only builder. Anchor = getAsOf() (real today/as-of, stable across month nav). parseKey(anchor) -> y,m,d. Loop i=0..6: dt=new Date(y,m,d+i); key=dateKey(dt.getFullYear(),dt.getMonth(),dt.getDate()) (native month/year rollover). Per day reuse: const cap=getCapacity(key) for dayUsed/dayFull/shift fullness (so the strip AGREES with the calendar's limit dots); onLeave=cap.dayUsed (active = pending+approved via isActiveLeave, rejected excluded). nonTrading=isWeekOffDate(key). blackout = (typeof isBlackoutDate==='function') ? isBlackoutDate(key) : false. Per-store (P1-28, feature-detected): bucket (data.leaves[key]||[]).filter(isActiveLeave) by store using P1-28 resolver, and derive available headcount per store from active master roster minus on-leave; understaffed = any store's available < that store's min-staff cap (or on-leave > maxLeave, per P1-28 caps semantics). If P1-28 helpers/caps absent -> skip understaffed highlight (never paint every day red). Non-trading suppresses understaffed (store closed => staffing moot). Build cells with DOM createElement/textContent (module XSS discipline; names not shown). Mark today's cell when key===todayISOStr().

specs.approach: Additive presentation layer with a hard dependency on P1-28. (1) Insert an empty #staffStrip container in the DOM under the stats strip. (2) Add scoped CSS reusing existing theme vars — no new colors, plus print-hide and mobile overflow. (3) Implement renderStaffStrip() that iterates the next 7 days from getAsOf(), reusing the EXISTING counting primitives getCapacity()/isActiveLeave() (pending+approved occupy capacity, rejected excluded — identical to the calendar's limit-dot logic) for the day total, isWeekOffDate() for non-trading marking, and P1-28's store resolver + per-store caps (feature-detected) for the per-store available-headcount and understaffed decision. (4) Append a single renderStaffStrip() call to renderCalendar()'s tail so the module's existing single-funnel refresh model drives it with no new event wiring. The whole change is one container + one CSS block + one function + one call line. It never mutates state, never changes a shared function signature, and never throws when P1-28 is absent (each P1-28 helper is guarded by typeof===\"function\").
specs.ui: Strip of 7 equal cells, horizontally scrollable on narrow screens. Each cell: day-of-week abbrev (Mon), date number, a primary count line 'N on leave', and a secondary 'M/T available' where T is the resolved store/total headcount. Today's cell gets an accent border; non-trading (weekly-off) cells get a muted/striped background with a small 'Weekly off' label and suppress the understaffed red; blackout cells (if P1-28/sibling provides isBlackoutDate) get an amber tint; understaffed cells get a red tint/left-border and a small '⚠ short' badge naming the short store when per-store data exists. Store-agnostic fallback (no P1-28 caps): show only 'N on leave' + non-trading marks, no red. Copy stays terse ('3 on leave', '5/7 avail', 'Weekly off', 'Short: Helios'). Read-only — no buttons, no click handlers required (optionally cell click could openDayModal(key) for the day, but keep display-only to stay strictly additive unless synthesis wants the affordance).
edgeCases: Build-order / P1-28 absent: if lvStoreCode/caps helpers are undefined (P1-30 merged before P1-28), every P1-28 call is guarded by typeof==="function"; strip falls back to a store-agnostic day view (total on-leave vs total active roster) and never throws.

Fresh install / empty saagar_employee_master_v1: getCentralEmployees() returns [] -> no roster -> available headcount unknown. Degrade: show on-leave counts + non-trading marks, SUPPRESS understaffed highlight (do not paint every day red).
Caps key absent on a populated install: feature-detect the P1-28 caps loader; if no thresholds, show counts without understaffed red.
Month/year rollover inside the 7-day window: handled by new Date(y,m,d+i) arithmetic + dateKey(); no manual month math.

Half-day leaves: getCapacity().dayUsed counts a half-day head as one absent head (consistent with the calendar's per-day cap). This slightly overstates availability loss; documented, kept simple for a compact strip.
Pending vs rejected: pending leaves ARE counted (they occupy capacity via isActiveLeave) so the strip matches the calendar limit dots; rejected are excluded.

Unassigned store ('' code): staff whose master row store text isn't Helios/Titan resolve to '' — follow grmStoreCode's no-fallback rule (never mislabel as Titan); exclude Unassigned from per-store understaffed math, show a separate tally only if non-zero.
Non-trading AND understaffed same day: non-trading wins visually (store closed) and suppresses the red.
On-leave exceeds store roster: clamp available at 0 (no negative numbers).
Past as-of (read-only view): strip is display-only anyway; still shows next-7 from the as-of date; no write path, no guardReadOnly needed.
Month navigation: because anchor=getAsOf(), prev/next month leave the strip content unchanged (it reflects 'now', not the browsed month) — intentional; documented as a decision.

specs.approach: Additive, read-only, mirror-the-neighbour. (1) Reuse the module's own month-key helper attFeedKey() (L3378) verbatim so the reconciliation buckets by the SAME calendar 'YYYY-MM' as the existing DSR feed — do NOT invent a second month-mapping. (2) Re-implement leave counting LOCALLY inside payroll.html (the modules are separate iframes and cannot call leave.html functions) but make it a faithful mirror of the leave desk's own counters: lrLeaveDays == leave.html leaveDaysOf (full_day→1 else 0.5) and lrCounts == leave.html isCountedLeave (approved OR legacy/no-status; pending & rejected excluded). Since submitLeave() expands multi-day leaves into ONE record per date key (leave.html L1912-1930, week-offs skipped), summing one record = lrLeaveDays per matching date key is exactly how the leave desk sums for its own FY balances (fyUsage L995-1006) — no leaveFrom/leaveTo span math needed. (3) Reconcile deskDays against row.leavesApplied (NOT absent): approved leave is the paid-leave axis that calcAttendance() adds back into salary days (L1696 finalPresent+leavesApplied+extraDays); absent is the unpaid-deduction axis and must NOT drive the mismatch flag (show it only as read-only context). (4) Placement mirrors renderAttFeedPanel exactly: a new <section class='validation'> sibling in pane-att with its own render fn wired into the same three att-render call sites plus the meta-change handler. (5) Recommend DISPLAY-ONLY (no write). Rationale: the module ALREADY has a guarded one-tap writer for leavesApplied via the DSR/Leave feed (prefillAttRow/applyAttFeedRows); adding a SECOND independent writer of the same field creates two 'sources of truth' and maker confusion. A pure cross-check that says 'Leave Desk says 3, you entered 2' lets the maker fix it by hand (or via the existing feed import) and is the lowest-risk satisfaction of 'one-tap reconciliation VIEW'.

specs.summary: Add a purely-derived, async evidence-completeness meter to the tax module. For the active firm + current FY it counts how many applicable (non-NA) obligations have their evidence "satisfied" — SaagarEvidence file count > 0 for evKey(itemId) OR a non-empty compliance evidenceRef — versus the required total, and surfaces an "X/Y have evidence" meter (with a missing-evidence drill list) on the dashboard, plus an optional per-month "Evidence" stat chip. No new localStorage key and no shell change required: it derives entirely from taxcal_v2 (STATE.compliance via getItemRecord/isItemDone/isItemNA + getVisibleItems/getMonthItems) and the existing shell SaagarEvidence IndexedDB store. Async aggregation mirrors hydrateEvidence — render a placeholder synchronously, fill after the promises resolve — with a firm/FY race guard so a slow promise from an old firm can never overwrite the new numbers.

(2) CAPTURE firmId=STATE.activeFirmId and fy=STATE.fyStartYear ONCE at the top and build keys as firmId+'|'+fy+'|'+id explicitly — do NOT call evKey() inside the async loop, because evKey() reads live STATE and would use the NEW firm/FY after a mid-flight switch. specs.approach: ADDITIVE and DERIVED-ONLY — no new localStorage key, no new record field, no shell edit strictly required. Every input already exists: (a) isItemNA(id)/isItemDone(id)/getItemRecord(id) read STATE.compliance[firmId][fy][id] out of taxcal_v2 (loadState ~851); (b) getVisibleItems(getMonthItems(m)) already yields the firm-type-filtered, archive-filtered, custom-inclusive obligation set per month (2443/2540); (c) the shell SaagarEvidence store (index.html ~4897) already exposes count(itemKey)->Promise<number> (line 4951) and evApi()=window.parent.SaagarEvidence (2905) already works cross-iframe (proven by hydrateEvidence). Satisfaction rule per obligation instance: satisfied = (getItemRecord(id).evidenceRef trimmed non-empty) OR (count(firmId|fy|id) > 0). This matches confirmDone() which writes evidenceRef AND attaches files (2946/2957/2960), and evAttachHere() which can attach files independent of a ref (2914). RECOMMENDED denominator = DONE non-NA obligations across the FY (headline: 'M of N completed filings have evidence'), because evidence only meaningfully exists once an item is filed — pending/future obligations legitimately have no proof yet, so including them would keep the meter perpetually low and non-actionable and conflate 'not yet due' with 'missing proof'. ALSO surface the FY-wide applicable-obligation total as a secondary context number, and make the drill-down 'missing evidence' list = done-but-unsatisfied rows (the true audit gaps). Granularity = one row per MONTHLY obligation instance (item ids are month-scoped and each has its own evKey bucket), so a monthly filing like GSTR-3B counts once per month with its own proof — the correct audit granularity. Async: build the row set synchronously, short-circuit rows already satisfied by a non-empty evidenceRef (no IndexedDB call), and Promise.all only the count() lookups for done-without-ref rows (a small set), then write the meter into a pre-rendered placeholder — exactly the hydrateEvidence lifecycle. Capture firmId+fy at compute start and guard the DOM write with a monotonic token so a firm/FY switch mid-flight cannot paint stale numbers.

specs.approach: ADDITIVE, read-only over evidence + display-only export — no writes to taxcal_v2, no writes to SaagarEvidence, no new key/field. Flow: SNAPSHOT → window.parent.SaagarEvidence.snapshotAll() returns [{itemKey,name,type,addedAt,dataURL}] across ALL firms/FYs/modules (it also holds watch photos keyed wsf|caseId). FILTER to the active scope with prefix = f.id+'|'+(STATE.fyStartYear||2026)+'|' and e.itemKey.indexOf(prefix)===0. This prefix is collision-safe because firm ids are 'firm_'+Date.now() (saveFirm@2038) and contain no '|', and it is byte-identical to evKey()@2904 which produced the keys — so no watch photo (wsf|...) or other firm/FY leaks in. ZIP BUILD: JSZipCtor=await ensureJSZipRef(); zip=new JSZipCtor(); for each file resolve meta=itemMetaById()[itemId] where itemId=itemKey.slice(prefix.length); folder = sanitize(meta ? meta.month+'_'+meta.cat+'_'+meta.name : itemId).slice(0,60) (append '__'+itemId only if two different obligations sanitize to the same folder — simplest robust rule: always suffix folder with a short itemId tail to guarantee uniqueness while staying readable); fname = sanitize(file.name||'evidence'); DEDUPE within a folder via a Set — on collision insert ' (2)', ' (3)' before the extension. Decode dataURL→Uint8Array (see helper), zip.folder(folder).file(fname, bytes). Optionally add a top-level index.csv/manifest.txt listing Obligation, Original filename, Stored path, Added-on (from addedAt) — recommended for 'audit-ready' but flag as an open question (nice-to-have vs. minimal). GENERATE blob (DEFLATE level 5, matching payroll's zip@1447) → downloadZipBlob() posts ST_SHARE with the Blob (Android-safe) / anchors on desktop. FILENAME: 'Evidence_'+sanitize(f.name||'firm')+'_'+getFinancialYearShortLabel()+'.zip', sanitized like exportComplianceCSV@2721 (replace(/[^\\w.-]+/g,'_').replace(/^_+|_+$/g,'')).

dataURL decode failure for one file (malformed/empty) → try/catch skip that file, keep a skipped counter; if EVERY file fails → treat as zero (alert). If some succeed, optionally note 'N file(s) skipped (unreadable)' in the success path.

itemId not resolvable to an obligation (custom item deleted, or item outside current FY catalogue) → folder falls back to the raw itemId (still a valid, unique folder).

The feed reader (getTaxPayableFeed / __taxPayFeed) and the per-card badge (taxPayableBadge/taxPayableAmount) already exist; P1-41 adds only new render helpers plus two insertion points. decisions.decision: DISPLAY-ONLY for v1. No write to leavedesk_v3 and no write to payroll state; no apply button.
decisions.rationale: The module already has a guarded one-tap writer of leavesApplied via the DSR/Leave feed (applyAttFeedRows). A second independent writer of the same field creates two sources of truth and maker confusion. A pure 'Leave Desk says N, you entered M' cross-check is the lowest-risk satisfaction of the requirement; the maker corrects by hand or via the existing feed import.

decisions.question: P1-31: reconcile leave desk against leavesApplied or absent?
decisions.decision: Reconcile deskDays against row.leavesApplied only. row.absent is shown as read-only context and never drives the mismatch flag.
decisions.rationale: Approved leave is the paid-leave axis calcAttendance@1687 adds back into salary days; absent is the unpaid-deduction axis. Flagging absent would be semantically wrong.

decisions.question: P1-33: how does the shell compute per-firm 'pending' without catalogue D?
decisions.decision: Read taxcal_v2.compliance[firmId][fy] records' dueDate/done/na directly (the same source computeTaxStatus and notifications already trust), via a new computeFirmTaxStatus(firmId,fy). Convert WA_CFG.tax to kind:'record' with a synthetic '__all' record + one record per firm.
decisions.rationale: materializeDueDates()@1154 persists a {dueDate,done:false,name} record for every visible obligation across all 12 months whenever the module renders — so the shell needs no catalogue. The synthetic '__all' record preserves today's owner-summary capability (no regression). firmMissing honest empty-state copy covers firms never opened in-module.

decisions.question: P1-35: advisory badge (Option A) vs filtering monthly/QRMP items in getVisibleItems (Option B).
decisions.decision: Option A — advisory badge + per-card notes, NO hiding/filtering. firms[i].qrmp is a nested boolean on taxcal_v2 (no top-level key).
decisions.rationale: Option B is a real correctness hazard: the SHELL Reports/notifications read compliance[fid][fy][itemId].dueDate DIRECTLY (bypassing getVisibleItems), so hidden-but-already-materialized monthly items would leak into Reports and double-count; it also strips the taxPayableField ₹ estimate and shifts dashboard scores. Option A keeps every score/count/Reports byte-identical.

decisions.question: P1-32: evidence-completeness denominator.
decisions.decision: DONE non-NA obligations ('M of N completed filings have evidence'), with FY-wide applicable total shown as secondary context; missing list = done-but-unsatisfied rows.
decisions.rationale: Evidence only meaningfully exists once an item is filed. Counting not-yet-due items as 'missing' keeps the meter perpetually low and conflates 'not yet due' with 'missing proof', making it non-actionable.

decisions.question: Store-code resolver: one shared helper or per-item clones?
decisions.decision: ONE shared resolver (lvStoreMap/lvStoreCode) owned by P1-28. P1-29 drops its proposed leaveStoreCode clone and consumes lvStoreCode; P1-30 consumes it too.
decisions.rationale: Three copies of the same grmStoreCode logic would drift. A single module-level resolver, with storeLeaveTallyForDay accepting a pre-built map, is cheaper and consistent.

decisions.question: P1-41: which month key for the statutory-payable card?
decisions.decision: Key the summary by the CURRENT real/as-of month (currentPayableYM mirroring the curMonth IIFE @2548), NOT taxPayableAmount()'s P-1 deposit-period shift. Fall back to the newest feed key with isCurrent=false labelling if the current month has no entry.
decisions.rationale: The bridge writes out[ym(today())] — the feed entry is keyed by the current month. The P-1 shift is correct only for per-deposit-line badges, and would show last month's figures on a 'what you owe this month' card.

decisions.question: P1-28 default per-store cap and enforcement posture.
decisions.decision: Default cap = MAX_DAY (3) per store; advisory-only (over-capacity FLAG in the day view), does NOT modify getCapacity/canAddLeave.
decisions.rationale: The global MAX_DAY=3 add-gate already binds; wiring per-store caps into add-gating would over-constrain and change existing semantics. Advisory keeps the wave additive and low-risk.

decisions.question: P1-29 store holiday (kind:'holiday') behaviour.
decisions.decision: Store holiday marks the calendar and warns in add-leave but is forced hard:false (never blocks) and does NOT auto-skip leave creation like weekly-off.
decisions.rationale: Auto-skip would need a store-aware variant of isWeekOffDate and would change leave counting for one store's employees — a bigger, non-additive change. Warn-only keeps counting untouched.

decisions.question: Bridge reconcileMasters store-carry one-liner: land this wave?
decisions.decision: Yes — land store:e.store||'' in the pushed lv.employees object. But no leave item may depend on it.
decisions.rationale: Additive and harmless; stamps store on newly-seeded leave employees for future convenience. The resolver reads the central master authoritatively regardless, so correctness never depends on it.
